text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- By the year-end Poland's treasury ministry plans capital privatisations of the Wolsztyn-based WZM furniture maker, the DT Centrum department store chain, the Radom tobacco plant, the Lezajsk brewery and two meat-processing plants in Elk and Tarnow, the deputy-minister in charge of privatisation, Wieslaw Kaczmarek, said.

- Only few high ranking civil servants and politicians have decided to make use of the blind trust financial services which will be available to them by December 1, to ensure impartiality and prevent insider dealing. Most politicians say they do not invest in stocks.

- Poland's Consumer Protection Office (UOK), which replaced the Anti-monopoly Office, has permitted the U.S. Ameritech telecom firm to sell a 24.5 percent stake in the Centertel analogue mobile phone company. Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecom monopolist, will increase its stake to 64 percent and France Telecom to 36 percent.
- Chio Lilly Snack Foods control 31 percent of Poland's potato chips market and almost 10 percent of all the snack foods market, company president Pawel Kosmala said.

- The Hortex food processor and trader will change into a public company next year, will raise capital and apply for listing on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (WSE) in 1999, its president Andrzej Szablewski said.
- The Pioneer Investment Fund has bought a 29 percent stake worth $4.7 million in the Alpex fibreboard plant in Karlino, northern Poland.
NOWA EUROPA
- Korea's Daewoo automaker plans to produce and sell 200,000 cars in Poland next year which will give it the biggest share in Poland's car market, Centrum Daewoo president Jung-Ho Choi said.
- France's Valeo car accessory maker has set up a Valeo Distribution company to introduce its products into Poland.
- More than 60 computer firms are exhibiting their products at the Krakow-based fourth Info-Festival which began yesterday.
- The Kielce-based KZWP paper plant, controlled by David Smith Kielce SA, has invested 2.5 million zlotys in a modern corrugated board packaging assembly line, technical director Jozef Zapala said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- German furniture makers' lobby spokesman Erich Neuman has expressed concern over low-cost imports to Germany from Poland and the Czech Republic, which he said endangered the existence of German small size furniture producers.

- Products such as beans and brooms are smuggled into Poland from Ukraine, electric water heaters come illegally from Belorussia, Scotch whisky from Slovakia and the Czech Republic and Christmas trees are smuggled through the sea-border, Poland's Main Customs Office said.
ZYCIE

- A crediting consortium organised by Bank Gdanski and including BIG SA bank will provide the Swinoujscie-based Porta-Petrol firm with a $19 million credit for its liquid fuel tank complex modernisation.
- Kredyt Bank (KB) officially announced that it has been granted an operating licence by the central bank of Lithuania. KB will be the first foreign bank to open a branch in that country.
PARKIET

- The Polski Bank Rozwoju (PBR) Polish development bank will guarantee the new B-share issue of the listed Energoaparatura electrical equipment maker. The company's share price inched up to 13 zlotys.
- The Merrill Lynch investment bank recommended buying shares of the Elektrim foreign trade company, BIG bank and Polifarb Cieszyn paint maker in its report dated October 30.
